applicability_conditions: Used for the modified Williamson-Hall analysis of synchrotron XRD line profiles of the ferrite and austenite phases in the present steel; A is set to 1 for both ferrite and austenite based on the value given in Ref. [61]. The equation is a series expansion in K C̄^1/2, valid to terms of higher order O(K²C̄).
purpose: Modified Williamson-Hall (MWH) equation that relates the broadening of diffraction peaks (ΔK) to microstructural parameters—the average crystalline/coherent domain size (L) and the dislocation density (ρ)—so that the dislocation density can be calculated from synchrotron X-ray diffraction line profiles.

symbols.meaning: Full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the corresponding diffraction peak plotted against K (the text writes '-K'), determined by fitting the peak with a pseudo-Voigt function
Average size of the coherently scattering domains, which corresponds to the average size of dislocation substructures (average crystalline size)
Constant determined by the outer cut-off radius of the dislocation; A > 1 indicates a random dislocation arrangement, while a value < 1 suggests a highly correlated arrangement
symbols.value: 1 (set to 1 for ferrite and austenite based on the value provided in Ref. [61])

symbols.meaning: Average dislocation contrast factor for a specific hkl reflection
Terms of higher order in the series expansion of the modified Williamson-Hall equation
Numerical coefficient of the size term 0.9/L in the Williamson-Hall-type expression (not explicitly explained in the text)

unmapped: The equation is the modified Williamson-Hall (MWH) method [59] used to calculate dislocation density from peak broadening [60].
Dislocation density is measured via synchrotron X-ray diffraction experiments on specimens before and after tensile tests (Fig. 10).
Three phases were identified in the line profiles: austenite (a_γ ≈ 0.368 nm), ferrite (a_δ ≈ 0.295 nm), and TiB (a_TiB2 ≈ 0.309 nm, c_TiB2 ≈ 0.328 nm).
